title: Wolf and Hollow
premise: Edmund Ishikawa owes the Thornfell temple ten years of service, but when the crown's witch-hunters arrive demanding a registry of the gifted, his hidden talent for hearing the mountains themselves becomes a death sentence. Fleeing with Vess, a disgraced huntress who once served the crown she now defies, Edmund seeks the Hollow Door — the last passage out of Thornfell, a province the crown erased from its maps after a failed rebellion. Betrayal strikes when Vess's former commander offers her pardon for Edmund's head, forcing her to choose between the law that raised her and the truth of what the crown did to Thornfell's gifted. In the end, they open the Door not to escape but to let the hunted through, and Edmund stays behind, his debt paid in a currency the temple never asked for: witness.
about_author: Cyrus Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping borderlands that no longer appear on official charts. Their fascination with erased places and the people who remember them fuels every story they tell.

chapters.title: The Registry of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Witch-hunters occupy the Thornfell temple, and Edmund must copy the very registry that will doom the gifted — while concealing his own name among them. When a child on the list vanishes, Edmund falsifies a line and knows his debt-bound life is over. The beat is quiet terror: the moment a careful man decides to be careless.

chapters.title: What the Huntress Carries
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to track the escaped scribe, Vess finds him half-dead on a smuggler's road and, instead of arresting him, follows him toward the Hollow Door she was told is a myth. Flashbacks reveal her role in Thornfell's suppression. The beat is uneasy alliance: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Crossing the high passes as winter falls, they find the Door guarded by the ghosts of the rebellion — and by Vess's commander, who offers her pardon for Edmund's head. She refuses; the hunters attack; the Door cracks open but not wide enough, and Edmund hears the mountain warn of an avalanche. The beat is sacrifice at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund holds the Door open with his gift while the hunted pass through, spending the hearing he was born with. Vess chooses to stay with him, her pardon burned on the wind. The avalanche buries the hunters; spring finds two fugitives rebuilding a temple of their own. The beat is costly, unregretted choice — justice outside the law.
